message.content:
Sure! Here’s a quick way to add that comment to the IP address **192.168.1.1** using the VirusTotal v3 API.  
Just run the following `curl` command (or adapt it to your preferred HTTP client).  

```bash
curl -X POST "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/192.168.1.1/comments" \
     -H "x-apikey: ABC321" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{
           "type": "comment",
           "attributes": {
             "text": "Confirmed #malware"
           }
         }'
```

**What this does**

| Part | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `POST https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/192.168.1.1/comments` | Target endpoint for adding a comment to the specified IP. |
| `-H "x-apikey: ABC321"` | Your API key (replace with your own if needed). |
| `-H "Content-Type: application/json"` | Tells VirusTotal that the payload is JSON. |
| `-d '{...}'` | The comment payload you supplied. |

**Python example (optional)**

```python
import requests

url = "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/192.168.1.1/comments"
headers = {
    "x-apikey": "ABC321",
    "Content-Type": "application/json"
}
payload = {
    "type": "comment",
    "attributes": {
        "text": "Confirmed #malware"
    }
}

response = requests.post(url, json=payload, headers=headers)
print(response.status_code)
print(response.json())
```

> **Note:**  
> * 192.168.1.1 is a private IP address; VirusTotal may not have public data for it, so the comment might be stored but not visible in the public feed.  
> * Keep your API key confidential—don’t share it publicly.
